semantic_conclusion.summary: All six obligations were independently assessed and all six proposed tests reviewed. Core selectors, dotfile matching, stable descendant symlink exclusion, broken-leaf behavior, explicit link following, and case rules are largely sound. F6 wrongly equates unreadable root with failing initial stat and misses uncaught walk iterator/context errors. Completeness and symlink claims need stable-tree/access/scope qualifications; T4 needs a real-denial precondition. No candidate edits, scientific rescue, ranking, cost inference, or native success judgment.

claim_groups.claim_group: F1 selector/scanning trace and multiple-** deduplication
claim_groups.assessment: rglob prepends **; _make_selector constructs recursive then leaf wildcard selectors; select_from checks the initial root with is_dir; recursion first yields that root, then uses walk; leaf scans call _scandir/os.scandir and buffer list(scandir_it). walk separately scans incrementally, so the wording each scan buffered should be confined to leaf scans. Non-adjacent ** selects the deduplicating subclass; adjacent ** is collapsed.

claim_groups.claim_group: F2 matching dotfiles
claim_groups.assessment: Name matching has no leading-dot exclusion. Pinned fnmatch translates *.csv to a regex equivalent to (?s:.*\.csv)\Z, supporting .hidden.csv, including beneath real dot-directories that are visited. This is source reasoning, not an executed 3.12.3 witness.

claim_groups.claim_group: F2 recursive symlink exclusion and blanket missing-subtree claims
claim_groups.assessment: Stable descendant directory symlinks are not placed in walk dirnames, hence are not recursively entered by bare *.csv. Never is too broad: the supplied root can itself be a directory symlink because is_dir/stat/scandir follow it; a real descendant replaced by a symlink after classification can still be entered. Link aliases are omitted, but a target also reachable through a real descendant can still contribute CSV files through that real path.

claim_groups.claim_group: F2/F4 explicit intermediate links and corpus counts
claim_groups.assessment: dironly selectors call entry.is_dir() with default follow_symlinks=True. Exact rglob fileB versus */fileB contrast is correct. test_glob_permissions creates 100 links, yields 100 for *, and 50 for */, */fileC, and */file*. Those tests are conditional on usable symlinks; reading their assertions does not mean running them.

claim_groups.claim_group: F3 broken links, leaf kinds, and long-target witness
claim_groups.assessment: The final leaf has dironly=False and no stat gate, so matching broken links, directory links, file links, and directories can all be yielded. Broken links used as intermediate components fail the directory predicate or are skipped on OSError. The loop test includes brokenLink/brokenLinkLoop; the long-link test uses bad repeated 200 times (600 characters) and expects bad_link.

claim_groups.claim_group: F4 loop immunity and 3.12.3 API switch
claim_groups.assessment: The stable descendant-link loop tests terminate because walk does not follow those links. The absolute immunity claim needs the mutation qualification in G03. No recurse_symlinks keyword exists in the pinned glob/rglob signatures; walk has follow_symlinks but rglob does not pass it. Finite explicit components may follow a directory link without turning each ** into link-following recursion.

claim_groups.claim_group: F5 platform/default/override case rules
claim_groups.assessment: The implementation chooses regex case sensitivity from path flavour via normcase, not by probing each directory. Defaults are sensitive for POSIX and insensitive for Windows; explicit True/False overrides. Thus X.CSV misses *.csv by default on POSIX and matches with False, including on a POSIX filesystem that happens to permit case-insensitive lookups. Pinning the flag stabilizes matching rules, not every platform-dependent filesystem behavior.

claim_groups.claim_group: F5 predicate error behavior
claim_groups.assessment: Listed ignored errnos and Windows errors are correct; other OSError from exists/is_dir propagates. The word only needs an OSError qualification: these predicates also return False on ValueError for non-encodable paths, and is_dir returns False for non-directories. The F5 mechanism does not establish the later root-unreadable claim.

claim_groups.claim_group: F6 suppression of scan-open and classification errors
claim_groups.assessment: Wildcard scanning suppresses OSError from opening/materializing/closing its scan. walk suppresses OSError when opening a directory with _scandir; on_error defaults to None. Entry is_dir OSError becomes False for walk classification, losing recursion into that entry; dironly wildcard entries are skipped. Ordinary access-denied opens therefore silently omit reachable results, including at the initial root after a successful is_dir check. rglob offers no on_error argument.

claim_groups.claim_group: F6 root-unreadable raises
claim_groups.assessment: Read permission on a directory is not required merely to stat that directory when its parent is searchable. An unreadable root can pass is_dir and then have both scans fail silently, yielding no CSV hits. Only non-ignored errors from the initial stat/is_dir gate propagate in that initial-check category; an inaccessible ancestor can cause that. Reviewer OS-only check observed stat success and scandir PermissionError for a mode-000 root, and stat PermissionError for a child beneath a mode-000 parent. Pinned source establishes the rglob consequence; CPython 3.12.3 rglob was not executed.

claim_groups.claim_group: F6 only the top-level gate can propagate / all nested scan OSError suppressed
claim_groups.assessment: walk catches only creation of scandir_it at line 1129. The with/for iteration at 1135-1138 is outside that handler, so OSError while entering, consuming, or exiting the opened walk scan can propagate through _iterate_directories and rglob. Leaf scan materialization does catch such OSError, making the two scan paths different. Docs generalize scan suppression, but released implementation governs this brief. This propagation is a control-flow conclusion conditional on an iterator/context operation raising; no filesystem I/O fault was injected.

claim_groups.claim_group: Recommendation/F7 completeness and post-filtering
claim_groups.assessment: Treating output as potentially partial is sound. Leaf results require an explicit object policy if the intended inventory includes only regular files: is_file follows file symlinks and can itself raise; lstat supplies link metadata but is not a filter by itself. Readable directories alone do not guarantee complete traversal: effective search/access rights through ancestors, no classification/scan failures, full consumption, and a stable tree matter. Two scans per visited directory provide no snapshot and can miss concurrent changes or enter replacement links. Clarify link-path versus unique-target inventory; skipping an alias need not lose a target reachable elsewhere. Candidate does not state these governing qualifications.

claim_groups.claim_group: Final self-dispositions and three rejected propositions
claim_groups.assessment: All six obligations are addressed and all seven findings are present, but accepted all seven / amended zero does not establish correctness. Rejecting dotfiles-excluded is correct. Rejecting universal recursive directory-link following is correct for stable descendants. Rejecting unreadable-subdirs-raise is correct for scan-open access denial, but the exception phrasing and universal suppression inherit G10/G11. No grading weight is assigned to the author self-labels.
